title: 2013 AMC 12A Problem 20
statement: Let \(S\) be the set \(\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 19\}.\) For \(a,\) \(b \in S,\) define \(a \succ b\) to mean that either \(0 \lt a - b \le 9\) or \(b - a \gt 9.\) How many ordered triples \((x, y, z)\) of elements of \(S\) have the property that \(x \succ y,\) \(y \succ z,\) and \(z \succ x?\)

solutions.text:
Reading the elements modulo \(19,\) the relation \(a \succ b\) holds exactly when \(0 \lt (a - b) \bmod 19 \le 9.\)

There are \(19\) choices for \(x.\) Once \(x\) is fixed, take \(y = x + i\) for some \(1 \le i \le 9.\) Then \(z\) must satisfy \(x + 10 \le z \le x + 9 + i,\) giving \(i\) choices.

The total is \(19(1 + 2 + \cdots + 9) = 19\cdot 45\) \(= 855.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Work modulo \(19;\) then \(a \succ b\) means \(0 \lt (a - b) \bmod 19 \le 9\)
Fix \(x\) (\(19\) ways); let \(y = x + i\) with \(1 \le i \le 9,\) then \(z\) has \(i\) options
